content:
Hi, we are researchers from PKU AI4Math team and IQuest Research @Xuanzhi Ren @Tony Beta Lambda @Ruitong Liu .

Here we're excited to bring our latest updates on reap tactic. We implement an AlphaProof-style MCTS algorithm for proof search in Lean, and reduce backend reaper model into 1.7B param size (could run on most modern laptops), achieving 80.3% accuracy on minif2f-test (state-of-the-art for models of this size).

This implementation makes reap not only as a neural tactic for daily use, but also a neat component in RL rollout recipe. For this purpose, we implement features like AND/OR proof states, per-tactic budget control, final assembling check and sufficient logging right inside Lean.

As researchers, we are long fascinated by how algorithms like MCTS can make great difference to automated theorem-proving (e.g. splendid work from AlphaProof and Aristotle). We hope this work could provide a kickstart and inspire curious researchers to explore more about reinforcement learning in native tactic proof search.

We have present our latest implementation inside reap repo. Our recent plan includes:

  • Refining our model before release so that it covers broader domain and can better serve daily use/agentic use
  • Using standard LibrarySuggestions API to support broader premise selectors

Feel free to read our blog or contact us if you are interested!

Repository link: https://github.com/frenzymath/reap
